flagged.evidence: The Statement claims that a residue-injective subfield K is contained in a coefficient field whenever k/rho(K) is purely inseparable. Let A=F_p(s)[[t]], m=(t), v=s^p+t, and K=F_p(v). Then K is residue-injective with rho(K)=F_p(s^p), while k=F_p(s) is purely inseparable over rho(K). If a coefficient field C contained K, its lift c in C of s would satisfy c^p=v, since c^p and v are both in C and have residue s^p. But every pth power in F_p(s)[[t]] lies in F_p(s^p)[[t^p]], so it has no t-term and cannot equal s^p+t. Thus no such C exists.

Step 3.1 says, “Then [L3] shows that K is contained in a coefficient field of A. Maximality forces that coefficient field to equal K.” Its cited L3 is the false purely-inseparable lemma. In A=F_p(s)[[t]], extend F_p(s^p+t) to a maximal residue-injective subfield. Its residue image cannot contain s, since that would give a pth root of s^p+t in A; hence its residue image is the proper field F_p(s^p). The invocation of L3 therefore does not license the conclusion that rho(K)=k.

The Statement asserts surjectivity for every continuous k-algebra map that is surjective modulo every m^n. Take k=F_p[t], A=F_p[[t]], m=(t), and phi:k[[X]] -> A defined by t maps to t and X maps to 0. This map is continuous, and each map to A/(t^n) is surjective because F_p[t] -> F_p[[t]]/(t^n) is surjective. But im(phi)=F_p[t], which omits 1+t+t^2+..., so phi is not surjective.

Step 1.1 displays “1=(-1)·T+1·(T-1) mod t”. The right-hand side is -T+T-1=-1, not 1 (for example over k=Q). Thus the asserted Bezout computation is false under the stated unrestricted field hypothesis.

[L1] states only that idempotents lift uniquely “in a Henselian pair,” but Step 2.1 applies it to the given “complete pair” without establishing or citing that (A,I) is Henselian. The claim can be closed by verifying I-adic completeness/separatedness and invoking cor-complete-separated-adic-pair-henselian.

[L1] applies to a Henselian local ring, while the Given data state only that k[[t]] is complete local. Step 1.1 invokes [L1] without establishing Henselianity or citing cor-complete-local-rings-are-henselian. That omitted link is enough to justify the application but is absent from the proof.
